title: Performance audit 2026-09-12: one SQLite writer is the product ceiling — land the audit fix map
description:
## Why this issue exists

Umbrella for the 2026-09-12 performance audit (plan `.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-12-performance-audit-admin-reorg/plan.md`; measurements in `docs/plans/reports/2026-09-12-A1-prod-measurement.md` and `docs/plans/reports/2026-09-12-A5-error-summary.md`). It tracks the audit as one deliverable so the individual fixes do not land as unrelated one-offs. Every number below was measured read-only on production; nothing was written, restarted or modified.

## What was measured

Window caveat: PM2 only began writing a leading ISO timestamp on 2026-09-09T11:31 UTC, so the log census covers **2.40 days (2026-09-09 18:31 BKK to 2026-09-12 04:05 BKK)**, not 7. Database and telemetry figures cover the full 14 Bangkok days to 2026-09-12.

* **219 transactions >= 2 s in 2.40 days (about 91/day), 217 of them >= 5 s.** Pooled p50 25,166 ms, p90 30,191 ms, max 46,302 ms. **150 of 219 (68.5 %) land within +/-500 ms of a configured timeout** (83 at the 20 s socket timeout, 67 at the 30 s transaction timeout).
* The host is idle while those requests wait: load <= 1.09 on 8 vCPU, 26.9 GB RAM free, event-loop p95 2.26 ms, HTTP mean 18 ms. This is queueing on one writer, not slow work.
* Named structural holder: `leaseStoryFilmGenerationJobs` (`src/lib/story-film-generation-queue.server.ts:224`) opens a write-first interactive transaction every `POLL_MS = 4000` ms, about 21,600 write transactions/day against a 114-row table; **65.2 % of its log lines fall inside a slow-transaction window, 36x baseline**.
* `TelemetryEvent` is **149.41 MB = 28.3 %** of the 527.52 MB live database (305,452 rows, 66 % older than 30 days), with no retention job. WAL high-water 35.2 MB = **8.54x** the autocheckpoint threshold, `journal_size_limit = -1`.
* 14-day error census: 95 of 1,119 video jobs failed (8.5 %); **413 of 520 `frontend_error` telemetry rows (79 %) are third-party browser noise** that `/admin/insights` counts as our own errors; RunPod `OUTPUT_INVALID` hit **20 users in 7 days** and is trending up.

## Scope

1. Remove the contention, not the error message. See the HERO-10 reopen comment for the metric that must move (`[prisma-slow-tx]` events >= 5,000 ms per Bangkok day, one line per event).
2. Telemetry retention plus noise filtering, so the database stops growing and `/admin/insights` stops counting browser-extension errors as ours.
3. Admin information architecture (Thai menu groups, daily trend cards, ADR 0062 money boundary).
4. Job Failure Class implemented once in `src/lib/job-failure-class.ts` and imported everywhere.

## Acceptance criteria

* Every task in the audit plan is landed or explicitly dropped with a reason recorded in this issue.
* `[prisma-slow-tx]` events >= 5,000 ms stay below 5 per Bangkok day for 7 consecutive days on both `ai-content` and `story-film-system-worker`.
* `TelemetryEvent` row count bounded by a retention job running in `ecosystem.config.js`.
* Before/after numbers filled in from the same read-only method as the audit (same commands, recorded in the report).

## Constraints carried from the audit

* Production stays read-only for measurement; only Mew deploys, and only when she says so.
* Render output is untouchable: no change to `src/remotion/**`, `src/lib/run-render.ts`, ffmpeg arguments, or `RENDER_*` / `STOCK_*` values.
* Schema changes are additive only (deploy runs `prisma db push`).
* No customer identity in any artefact produced under this issue.
